newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open higher after polls.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open higher after polls.

text.p: French stocks opened higher on Monday, bolstered by two polls giving the ruling centre-right coalition a sizeable majority in the upcoming parliamentary election.
The bourse was also underpinned by the dollar's strength, but its advance was muted by caution ahead of a string of U.S. economic indicators due out this week, brokers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 13.69 points, or 0.54 percent, at 2,549.95 at 0840 GMT. The CAC-40 April futures contract was 15 points higher at 2,550.
Volume was a modest 450 million francs.

A Sofres poll published in Monday's Le Figaro sees the centre-right winning the May 25-June 1 election with 329 seats, the Socialists, other left and ecologists obtaining 202, the Communists 23 and the National Front one of 555 seats.

An IFOP poll published on Sunday in the Journal du Dimanche showed the RPR-UDF coalition and conservative allies winning between 311 and 331 National Assembly seats, the Socialists between 200 and 220, Communists between 19 and 25.
The two polls provided some reassurance to French financial markets, which were jolted last week by a poll predicting a tight race.
Brokers say investors are hoping for a majority of 310 seats or more.
But a BVA poll for France 2 TV and Europe 1 radio issued on Monday morning said that if the election were held now, the ruling RPR-UDF coalition would win 296 seats.
Casino shares rose 3.03 percent to 265.30 francs. Chairman Georges Plassat said in an interview in Les Echos that the hypermarkets group must grow to be able to compete with Carrefour.
